package fx;

import io.github.graphmaquina.api.MachineObserver;
import io.github.graphmaquina.runtime.MachineRegistry;
import io.github.graphmaquina.runtime.StateMachines;
import java.util.Objects;
import java.util.concurrent.Executor;
import java.time.InstantSource;
import io.github.graphmaquina.annotation.internal.GeneratedCompanion;

/** Generated set of {@link Library}: builds the registry once and hands out the facades. Do not edit. */
@GeneratedCompanion
@SuppressWarnings({"deprecation", "removal", "rawtypes"})
public final class LibraryRuntime implements Library {

    private final MachineRegistry machineRegistry;
    private final Docs docs;

    private LibraryRuntime(MachineRegistry machineRegistry) {
        this.machineRegistry = machineRegistry;
        this.docs = new DocsRuntime(machineRegistry.of(DocsRuntime.KEY));
    }

    /**
     * Starts a builder of the set over every class with instance members the machines use.
     *
     * @param docActions the {@code fx.DocActions} whose instance members the machines call
     * @return a new builder of the set
     */
    public static Builder builder(DocActions docActions) {
        return new Builder(docActions);
    }

    /**
     * Mirrors MachineRegistry.Builder and StateMachines.Builder, which it creates with itself and hands
     * every setting to as soon as it is given: what they refuse is refused where it is given, and
     * observers add up in the order they are given. Single-use and not thread-safe: once build()
     * succeeded, nothing is accepted.
     */
    public static final class Builder {

        private final MachineRegistry.Builder registry = MachineRegistry.builder();
        private final StateMachines.Builder<Doc, DocStatus, DocTransition> docsBuilder;
        private boolean used;

        private Builder(DocActions docActions) {
            Objects.requireNonNull(docActions, "docActions");
            this.docsBuilder = StateMachines.from(DocsRuntime.graph(docActions))
                    .state((Doc entity) -> entity.getStatus(), (Doc entity, DocStatus state) -> entity.setStatus(state))
                    .identity((Doc entity) -> entity.id())
                    .as(Docs.class);
            registry.add(docsBuilder);
        }

        /**
         * Hands the given executor to the StateMachines.Builder of every machine of the set, whose calls
         * submitted through async(...) then run on it, as StateMachines.Builder.asyncExecutor(Executor)
         * describes.
         *
         * @param executor the executor of those calls
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder asyncExecutor(Executor executor) {
            checkUnused();
            Objects.requireNonNull(executor, "executor");
            docsBuilder.asyncExecutor(executor);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Records the trail of every call through the set on the set's clock, the one clock(InstantSource)
         * gives or InstantSource.system(), by calling recordTrail() on the StateMachines.Builder of every
         * machine of the set. The root machine of a call decides for the whole call, so every root call made
         * through the set records its trail, the peers it cascades to and the exits of sub-machines its steps
         * run included, and so does each watch reaction, a call of its own that its own machine, one of the
         * set, decides. The flow such a call hands out, in its outcome or in its failure, lists in trail()
         * each hop and each sub-machine start the call took, each at the instant that clock read right after
         * the call took it, then the rejection or the failure that ended the call, at the instant it ended. A
         * call that records its trail creates its flow when its step starts, so it hands out its flow, with
         * the root entity and the trail, even when none of its steps or hooks wrote to it; an ignored outcome
         * hands out the empty flow: a reevaluation that selects no edge and an advance whose state has no
         * automatic edge run no step, and an advance whose automatic edges were all refused, or a choice whose
         * candidates were all refused, wrote nothing. The clock is read on the thread running the call, once
         * per entry the call appends, an entry a rollback later drops included, so a clock that advances on
         * each read leaves a gap for each dropped entry. Anything but an Error that the clock throws, a
         * checked exception included, fails the call as what an identity function throws does: the entry it
         * could not mark is left out of the trail. When it throws while the call reads the instant of the
         * Failed entry that ends a failed call, whatever failed the call, the call's CallFailedException
         * carries what it threw as suppressed, unless it threw that very exception, and its trail ends without
         * that entry; an InterruptedException suppressed there interrupts the thread again, and an Error
         * propagates. A clock that answers null counts as one that throws a NullPointerException. A set built
         * without recordTrail keeps no mark.
         *
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder recordTrail() {
            checkUnused();
            docsBuilder.recordTrail();
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Sets the clock of every machine of the set, by handing the given clock to the StateMachines.Builder
         * of every machine of the set; InstantSource.system() by default. The now() of a guard's or an
         * action's context reads it once per request: the first time a context of a root call or of a check
         * asks, and every later now() of the same call answers that same instant, in the steps it cascades to,
         * the exits its steps run and the checks its guards start. A check of its own, a choice check for all
         * its candidates, a watch reaction and each automatic attempt read it again, and a call that never
         * asks reads no clock. Anything but an Error that the clock throws, and a null instant, refused with a
         * NullPointerException, is thrown by now() to the guard or the action that asked. A set that records
         * its trail reads its trail on this clock too. A test can pass a clock it controls, such as a
         * java.time.Clock.
         *
         * @param clock the clock of every machine of the set
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder clock(InstantSource clock) {
            checkUnused();
            Objects.requireNonNull(clock, "clock");
            docsBuilder.clock(clock);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Bounds how deep a cascade may go, the root being at depth 0. The exit of a sub-machine counts at its
         * own depth: one level below the step that ended the child or, when the child stood in a terminal
         * state while its parent was still running the step that entered the bound state, one level below that
         * step. The default is 10, and a value below 1 is refused.
         *
         * @param depth the deepest level a cascade may reach, at least 1
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder maxCascadeDepth(int depth) {
            checkUnused();
            registry.maxCascadeDepth(depth);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Bounds how many watch reactions may follow one another; the default is 10, and a value below 1 is
         * refused. A call that an after-commit hook starts is a new root, which this bound never counts: the
         * watch reactions it triggers begin a chain of their own, so hooks that keep starting calls recur
         * until the stack of the thread overflows, as MachineRegistry says.
         *
         * @param chain how many watch reactions may follow one another, at least 1
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder maxWatchChain(int chain) {
            checkUnused();
            registry.maxWatchChain(chain);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Bounds how many automatic attempts that commit something may follow one another on one path of
         * continuations from a call of the application; the default is 10, and a value below 1 is refused. The
         * attempt past the bound that admits a candidate aborts before its action, writing nothing, with an
         * AutomaticChainExceededException. A call that an after-commit hook starts is a new root, which this
         * bound never counts.
         *
         * @param chain how many automatic attempts may follow one another, at least 1
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder maxAutomaticChain(int chain) {
            checkUnused();
            registry.maxAutomaticChain(chain);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Adds an observer of every call of the set; observers add up and are notified in the order they are
         * given.
         *
         * @param observer the observer to add
         * @return this builder
         */
        public Builder observer(MachineObserver observer) {
            checkUnused();
            registry.observer(observer);
            return this;
        }

        /**
         * Builds the registry of the machines and the set over it, which hands out their facades. Once it
         * succeeds, the builder accepts nothing more.
         *
         * @return the set
         */
        public Library build() {
            checkUnused();
            LibraryRuntime built = new LibraryRuntime(registry.build());
            used = true;
            return built;
        }

        /** Refuses any use once build() has succeeded: a built set is neither rebuilt nor reconfigured. */
        private void checkUnused() {
            if (used) {
                throw new IllegalStateException("this LibraryRuntime.Builder was already used");
            }
        }
    }

    @Override
    public Docs docs() { return docs; }

    @Override
    public void close() { machineRegistry.close(); }
}
